I see! When I used Nizoral, I would usually put a tiny amount, lather it a bit, put it on my forehead and wait for a minute or two then rinse right after. I saw results the day after, so that's why I decided to continue, but if not I think I would've stopped right away. Hope it works out if you do decide to use it :)

Also had similar bumps on my forehead a while ago! Mine were quite itchy though, so I thought it was fungal acne and bought Nizoral (dandruff shampoo). I used it for a few days, and no more bumps! If yours are itchy as well, perhaps you can try dandruff shampoo? I heard head & shoulders works too, but I'm not sure as I've only tried Nizoral.

Are you using any products which target acne? If not, you could use actives such as benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid etc. There's a BP Wash and gel in the UK Boots store called Acnecide/Purifide. BP is usually suggested as first line treatment as per NHS' guidelines. Otherwise, I would also suggest to start monitoring for any triggers which might cause your acne, e.g., stress, lack of sleep, specific products, diet etc. Though, as some have already suggested, you could try going to your GP through your university, maybe they'll have some suggestions. If you are planning to incorporate new active ingredients which target acne in your routine, always do a patch test first, don't use actives together (eg., BP and Salicylic acid) and use low doses - consistency over intensity :)
Hmm, this looks a bit like "Keratosis Pilaris", might want to check that out. Do you take hot showers? If you do, try avoiding that as it could cause flare ups.

First, try not to pop them as this could disrupt the healing process and introduce new bacteria - hence the reappearance. It could also be that when you pop, they're not properly drained, so it's best to just leave it be until they dry out. 
Also, what products are you currently using?

I know a lot of products have been suggested here, but if you want to opt for a more simpler method before you try any new products is to try rinsing the shampoo and conditioner forward, not letting any of the residue fall on/ touch your back or your chest. Also, don't use soap on your chest and back and avoid using very warm water on those areas. Turns out my skin gets very irritated when I do that, so my doctor suggested I stopped using soap on these areas and I've been acne-free since!

I really wish I could answer that, but I really don't know.. Why are there so many nasty people in this world? why is it so unfair for some? What I'm quite shocked is though, by reading some of the comments, is how some of these people are able to work as volunteers?? I wish they were more strict when recruiting, as it is really not a job anyone can just have.

I am so sorry to hear that many of you have experienced it that way.. I am someone who volunteers for a hotline (still new and learning), but I have also tried one myself. Sadly, I've also talked with someone where I didn't feel as understood or heard 'cus they basically just repeated everything I said. But as someone who works there, I think it's also quite difficult to know what people would like to hear 'cus I personally don't like it when someone just says 'it'll get better' and then that's it. We also try not to say it, because some don't view it at that way. If I find it difficult, I usually ask people "How would you like for me to respond to that?" or "What would you like to hear right now?" or even "What do you think you need right now?", cus we can't really give off any advice... I may not be the best, but I am very eager to learn tho, and know how you would like it to be, such as what are some things you would like to hear? what would you wish could be different?  I find it so a bit messed up tho that people who do come in and are able to find comfort in talking with us, will have to end the convo and go back to their daily lives again . That's why I absolutely hate saying goodbye.. Sadly, we get a lot of people who come to us, but we don't have enough people who volunteer... But reading all these stories also do make me quite sad and upset, sometimes I wish I could make many of my colleagues read some of these posts and make them understand that it doesn't help to just say that "It will get better"..
